## [0.44.0] - 2026-10-17

Nothing to read before updating. This release makes load-test results easier to
trust and compare, adds Insomnia v5 import and Postman environment export, and
makes the first ten minutes smoother: a clearer welcome screen, curl paste, and
a fallback port when 9876 is taken.

### Added

- **Insomnia v5 import.** Collections and environments exported as Insomnia v5
  YAML import alongside the existing formats.
- **Compare any two runs.** A run in History can be compared with any other run
  of the same request, with a warning when the two are not like for like, and a
  p95, throughput and error-rate trend across a request's runs.
- **A verdict on every load run.** A finished run says whether it passed, on the
  run itself and on its History row, and says so when the run was stopped.
  Budgets carried over from a request are visible in the load-test dialogs and
  tagged in the verdict.
- **One report for a finished run.** The dashboard shows History's report,
  including the HDR plot, per-sample and slow-request views. The Samples tab
  sorts by time, filters by status class, and error rows in the Overview link to
  an example.
- **Export a run as JSON.** `POST /export/run-report` returns a finished load run
  as a file.
- **Export an environment as a Postman environment** from the environment row
  menu.
- **Vayu's own time per request.** The response bar shows how much of a request's
  time was Vayu's, not the server's.
- **Import anywhere.** Drop a file anywhere on the window to open the Import
  dialog. Paste a curl command into the Import dialog or the URL bar to open it
  as a request. The preview says which variables, auth and scripts came along,
  and the import notes stay reachable inside the imported collection.
- **A clearer first run.** The welcome screen says what Vayu is for and offers
  to connect a coding agent, and its New request tile works. If port 9876 is
  taken, Vayu starts on another port and tells you which one to free.
- **Load-test dialog.** It names the target host and advises when it is not on
  your network, shows a two-pane layout, and offers a collection load test the
  same profiles as a request. "Virtual users" is the one name for the user
  count. Fixed Iterations is now Fixed request count.
- **MCP.** The server runs on SDK v2 for both protocol eras.
- **`install.sh`** offers to open Vayu after a fresh install and refuses macOS
  older than 13.3.

### Changed

- The live error rate counts HTTP error responses, the same way every report and
  MCP tool does.
- Runs are named Send, Collection run and Load test across History, the palette
  and the welcome screen.
- The request and response tab strips fit the pane and move the rest into a
  menu.
- An imported Postman environment is activated when none was.

### Fixed

- Requests cancelled by Stop are counted apart from errors.
- A finished run no longer reports a lost live metrics stream.
- Scenario steps count HTTP error responses in their Errors tally, and replay
  every enabled post-request script, never a disabled one.
- Sub-millisecond latencies print as such instead of "0 ms"; latency percentiles
  and idle virtual users are no longer painted as failures; chart axes start at
  zero and carry a unit.
- Counts and rates are grouped the same way on every run screen.
- A request rate below 10 req/s keeps a decimal instead of showing 0.
- The import loss report stays after a successful import.
- A root folder's badge counts its descendant requests.
- A file the OS hands Vayu opens in the Import dialog even when it is already
  open.
- Internal: a vcpkg baseline bump (curl 8.23.0), documentation and comparison
  pages brought back in line with the code, and test and refactoring work.
